summary: A nostalgic feature by Taylor Greene (published September 8, 2023) celebrating autumn cooking built on root vegetables and orchard fruits. It moves through history, orchard traditions, soups and stews, sweets, harvest festivals, health benefits, roasting, and preserving, quoting chefs, bakers, historians and a dietitian. The central theme is that seasonal food links communities to heritage, memory and family.
one_line: Taylor Greene's 2023 article celebrates autumn root vegetables and orchard fruits through recipes, events, expert quotes, and themes of nostalgia, heritage, health and preserving.
key_facts: The article was published on September 8, 2023, by Taylor Greene under Regional Cuisine and Recipes.
Culinary historian Joyce Edwards says turnips, parsnips, and sweet potatoes are 'a link to our past'.
On October 12, 2023, Chef Michael Harris demonstrated roasting carrots, beets, and rutabagas at the local Farmers' Market.
Pastry chef Emily Martin calls heirloom apples, pears, and quinces 'storytellers of the season'.
On September 17, 2023, families gathered at Henderson's Orchard for the annual apple-picking event.
Grandma Elsie's Beef and Parsnip Stew is a cherished recipe shared by food blogger Stephanie Larson; the recipe dates back to October 5, 1962.
On November 3, 2023, the bakery Sweet Seasons unveiled its 'Orchard's Bounty' collection; head baker Samantha Torres described pie-making as a seasonal ritual.
The annual Autumn Harvest Feast on September 30, 2023, featured root vegetable and orchard fruit dishes made with local farmers and artisans.
Culinary anthropologist Dr. Jacob Miller says food-centric festivals are a tableau on which cultural and personal histories are painted.
Root vegetables are rich in fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants, while orchard fruits provide vitamin C; dietitian Anna Young says 'Eating seasonally is eating smartly'.
On October 21, 2023, the aroma of roasting butternut squash and spiced apples wafted from neighborhood homes.
Mary Jensen has canned apple butter every fall for nearly fifty years and sees preserving as storytelling.
